paragraphs.text_en: Articles were eligible for inclusion if published in peer-reviewed journals, with no restrictions in language or publication date. The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines were adopted. Participants, interventions, comparators, outcomes, and study design (P.I.C.O.S.) were established as follows: (i) Participants with no restriction regarding health, sex, age, or training status; (ii) ST interventions supervised by a certified professional. ST was defined as any method focused on developing strength, ranging from resistance training to plyometrics; no limitations were placed with regard to intensity, volume, type of contractions and frequency, as it could excessively narrow the searches; (iii) comparators were supervised groups performing any form of stretching, including static stretching, passive stretching, dynamic stretching, and PNF, regardless of their intensity, duration or additional features; (iv) outcomes were ROM assessed in any joint, preferably through goniometry, but standardized tests such as the sit-and-reach were also acceptable; (v) randomized controlled trials (RCTs). RCTs reduce bias and better balance participant features between the groups, and are important for the advancement of sports science. There were no limitations regarding intervention length.

Были приняты руководящие принципы «Предпочтительные пункты отчетности для систематических обзоров и метаанализов» (PRISMA). Участники, вмешательства, компараторы, результаты и дизайн исследования (P.I.C.O.S) были установлены следующим образом: (i) участники без ограничений в отношении здоровья, пола, возраста или статуса обучения; (ii) вмешательства ST, контролируемые сертифицированным специалистом. ST был определен как любой метод, ориентированный на развитие силы, начиная от тренировки сопротивления до плиометрии; никаких ограничений в отношении интенсивности, объема, типа сокращений и частоты не было установлено, поскольку он мог чрезмерно сузить поиски. (iii) компараторы были контролируемыми группами, выполняющими любую форму растяжения, включая статическое растяжение, пассивное растяжение, динамическое растяжение и PNF, независимо от их интенсивности, продолжительности или дополнительных особенностей; (iv) результаты были оценены в любом суставе, предпочтительно с помощью гониометрии, но стандартизированные тесты, такие как сит-и-достижение, также были приемлемыми; v) рандомизированные контролируемые испытания (РКИ). paragraphs.section_en: 2. Materials and Methods / 2.3. Information Sources and Search
paragraphs.text_en: Six databases were used to search and retrieve the articles in early October 2020: Cochrane Library, EBSCO, PubMed (including MEDLINE), Scielo, Scopus, and Web of Science (Core Collection). Boolean operators were applied to search the article title, abstract and/or keywords: (“strength training” OR “resistance training” OR “weight training” OR “plyometric*” OR “calisthenics”) AND (“flexibility” OR “stretching”) AND “range of motion” AND “random*”. paragraphs.text_en: Data items: (i) Population: subjects, health status, sex/gender, age, training status, selection of subjects; (ii) intervention and comparators: Study length in weeks, weekly frequency of the sessions, weekly training volume in minutes, session duration in minutes, number of exercises per session, number of sets and repetitions per exercise, load (e.g., % 1 Repetition Maximum), full versus partial ROM, supervision ratio; in the comparators, modality of stretching applied was also considered; adherence rates were considered a posteriori; (iii) ROM testing: joints and actions, body positions (e.g., standing, supine), mode of testing (i.e., active, passive, both), pre-testing warm-up, timing (e.g., pre- and post-intervention, intermediate assessments), results considered for a given test (e.g., average of three measures), data reliability, number of testers and instructions provided during testing; (iv) Outcomes: changes in ROM for intervention and comparator groups; (vi) funding and conflicts of interest.

paragraphs.text_en: Meta-analysis was conducted when ≥3 studies were available. When means and SDs were not available, they were calculated from 95% confidence intervals (CIs) or standard error of mean (SEM), using Cochrane’s RevMan Calculator for Microsoft Excel. When ROM data from different groups (e.g., men and women) or different joints (e.g., knee and ankle) was pooled, weighted formulas were applied.

paragraphs.section_en: 2. Materials and Methods / 2.10. Synthesis of Results
paragraphs.text_en: The inverse variance random-effects model for meta-analyses was used to allocate a proportionate weight to trials based on the size of their individual standard errors, and accounting for heterogeneity across studies. The ESs were presented alongside 95% CIs and interpreted using the following thresholds: <0.2, trivial; 0.2–0.6, small; >0.6–1.2, moderate; >1.2–2.0, large; >2.0–4.0, very large; >4.0, extremely large. Heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 statistic, with values of <25%, 25–75%, and >75% considered to represent low, moderate, and high levels of heterogeneity, respectively. Data used for meta-analysis is available in a supplementary Excel file.

ESs были представлены вместе с 95% CI и интерпретированы с использованием следующих порогов: <0.2, тривиальный; 0.2-0.6, маленький; >0.6-1.2, умеренный; >1.2-2.0, большой; >2.0-4.0, очень большой; >4.0, чрезвычайно большой. Неоднородность оценивалась с использованием статистики I2, при этом значения <25%, 25-75% и >75%, как считается, представляют собой низкие, умеренные и высокие уровни неоднородности соответственно. paragraphs.text_en: Although not planned in the registered protocol, we decided to abide by the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE), which addresses five dimensions that can downgrade studies when assessing the quality of evidence in RCTs. paragraphs.text_en: An initial search returned 194 results (52 in Cochrane Library, 11 in EBSCO, 11 in PubMed, 9 in Scielo, 88 in Scopus, and 23 in Web of Science). After removal of duplicates, 121 records remained. Screening the titles and abstracts for eligibility criteria resulted in the exclusion of 106 articles: 26 were not original research articles (e.g., trial registrations, reviews), 24 were out of scope, 48 did not have the required intervention or comparators, five did not assess ROM, two were non-randomized and one was unsupervised. Fifteen articles were eligible for full-text analysis. One article did not have the required intervention, and two did not have the needed comparators. In one article, the ST and stretching groups performed a 20–30 min warm-up following an unspecified protocol. In another, the intervention and comparator were unsupervised, and in one the stretching group was unsupervised. Finally, in one article, 75% of the training sessions were unsupervised. Therefore, eight articles were included at this stage.

paragraphs.text_en: A manual search within the reference lists of the included articles revealed five additional potentially fitting articles. Two lacked the intervention group required, and two were non-randomized. One article met the inclusion criteria. Four experts revised the inclusion criteria and the list of articles and suggested eight articles based on their titles and abstracts. Six were excluded: interventions were multicomponent; comparators performed no exercise; out of scope; and unsupervised stretching group. Two articles were included, increasing the list to eleven articles, with 452 participants eligible for meta-analysis (Figure 1). Updated searches: in the renewed searches, 28 records emerged, of which two passed the screening. However, these two records had already been included in our final sample. In two articles, none of the groups improved ROM.

paragraphs.text_en: From the five articles, including both genders, four provided pooled data, with no distinction between genders. One article presented data separated by gender, without significant differences between men and women in response to interventions. Weighted formulas were applied sequentially for combining means and SDs of groups within the same study. Two studies presented the results separated by left and right lower limbs, with both showing similar responses to the interventions; outcomes were combined using the same weighted formulas for the means and SDs. Five articles only presented one decimal place, and so all values were rounded for uniformity.
paragraphs.text_ru_machine: Из пяти статей, в том числе по обоим признакам пола, четыре представляли сводные данные без каких-либо различий между полами. В одной статье были представлены данные, разделенные по полу, без существенных различий между мужчинами и женщинами в ответ на вмешательства. Весовые формулы применялись последовательно для объединения средств и СД групп в рамках одного исследования. В двух исследованиях были представлены результаты, разделенные левой и правой нижними конечностями, причем оба показали аналогичные ответы на вмешательства; результаты были объединены с использованием одних и тех же взвешенных формул для средств и SD. Пять статей представляли только одно десятичное место, и поэтому все значения округлялись для однородности.

paragraphs.text_en: The aim of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to compare the effects of supervised and randomized ST compared to stretching protocols on ROM, in participants of any health and training status. Qualitative synthesis showed that ST and stretching interventions were not statistically different in improving ROM. However, the studies were highly heterogeneous with regard to the nature of the interventions and moderator variables, such as gender, health, or training status. This had been reported in the original manuscripts as well. A meta-analysis, including 11 articles and 452 participants, showed that ST and stretching interventions were not statistically different in active and passive ROM changes, regardless of RoB in the randomization process, or in measurement of the outcome. RoB was low for deviations from intended interventions, missing outcome data, and selection of the reported results. No publication bias was detected.

Качественный синтез показал, что ST и растягивающие вмешательства статистически не отличаются в улучшении ПЗУ. Тем не менее, исследования были весьма неоднородными в отношении характера вмешательств и модераторов переменных, таких как пол, здоровье или статус обучения. Об этом также сообщалось в оригинальных рукописях. Мета-анализ, включающий 11 статей и 452 участника, показал, что ST и растягивающие вмешательства не отличались статистически в активных и пассивных изменениях ПЗУ, независимо от RoB в процессе рандомизации или в измерении результата. paragraphs.text_en: High heterogeneity is expected in continuous variables, such as ROM. However, more research should be conducted to afford sub-group analysis according to characteristics of the analyzed population, as well as protocol features. For example, insufficient reporting of training volume and intensity meant it was impossible to establish effective dose-response relationships, although a minimum of five weeks of intervention, and two weekly sessions were sufficient to improve ROM. Studies were not always clear with regard to the intensity used in ST and stretching protocols. Assessment of stretching intensity is complex, but a practical solution may be to apply scales of perceived exertion, or the Stretching Intensity Scale. ST intensity may also moderate effects on ROM, and ST with full versus partial ROM may have distinct neuromuscular effects and changes in fascicle length. Again, the information was insufficient to discuss these factors, which could potentially explain part of the heterogeneity of results. This precludes advancing stronger conclusions and requires further research to be implemented.
paragraphs.text_ru_machine: Высокая гетерогенность ожидается в непрерывных переменных, таких как ПЗУ. Тем не менее, необходимо провести дополнительные исследования, чтобы обеспечить анализ подгрупп в соответствии с характеристиками анализируемой популяции, а также особенностями протокола. Например, недостаточная отчетность об объеме и интенсивности тренировок означала, что невозможно установить эффективные соотношения доза-реакция, хотя для улучшения ПЗУ было достаточно как минимум пяти недель вмешательства и двух еженедельных сессий. Исследования не всегда были ясны в отношении интенсивности, используемой в протоколах ST и растяжения. Оценка интенсивности растяжения сложна, но практическим решением может быть применение шкалы воспринимаемой нагрузки или шкалы интенсивности растяжения. Интенсивность ST может также умеренно влиять на ROM, а ST с полным и частичным ROM может иметь различные нервно-мышечные эффекты и изменения длины фасциклов. Опять же, информации было недостаточно для обсуждения этих факторов, что потенциально могло бы объяснить часть неоднородности результатов. Это исключает продвижение более сильных выводов и требует дальнейших исследований.

paragraphs.text_en: Most studies showed ROM gains in ST and stretching interventions, but in two studies, neither group showed improvements. Although adherence rates were unreported by Aquino, Fonseca, Goncalves, Silva, Ocarino and Mancini, they were above 91.7% in Leite, De Souza Teixeira, Saavedra, Leite, Rhea and Simão, thus providing an unlikely explanation for these results. In the study by Aquino, Fonseca, Goncalves, Silva, Ocarino and Mancini, the participants increased their stretch tolerance, and the ST group changed the peak torque angle, despite no ROM gains. The authors acknowledged that there was high variability in measurement conditions (e.g., room temperature), which could have interfered with calculations. Leite, De Souza Teixeira, Saavedra, Leite, Rhea and Simão suggested that the use of dynamic instead of static stretching could explain the lack of ROM gains in the stretching and stretching + ST groups. However, other studies using dynamic stretching have shown ROM gains. Furthermore, Leite, De Souza Teixeira, Saavedra, Leite, Rhea and Simão provided no interpretation for the lack of ROM gains in the ST group.

paragraphs.text_en: Globally, however, both ST and stretching were effective in improving ROM. We asked what the reason for ST to improve ROM in a manner that is not statistically distinguishable from stretching? A first thought might be to speculate that perhaps the original studies used sub-threshold stretching intensities and/or durations. However, the hypothesis that ST has intrinsic merit for improving ROM should also be considered. ST with an eccentric focus demands the muscles to produce force on elongated positions, and a meta-analysis showed limited-to-moderate evidence that eccentric ST is associated with increases in fascicle length. Likewise, a recent study showed that 12 sessions of eccentric ST increased fascicle length of the biceps femoris long head. However, ST with an emphasis in concentric training has been shown to increase fascicle length when full ROM was required. In a study with nine older adults, ST increased fascicle length in both the eccentric and concentric groups, albeit more prominently in the former. Conversely, changes in pennation angle were superior in the concentric group (35% increase versus 5% increase). Plyometric training can also increase plantar flexor tendon extensibility.

paragraphs.text_en: One article showed significant reductions in pain associated with increases in strength. Therefore, decreased pain sensitivity may be another mechanism by which ST promotes ROM gains. An improved agonist-antagonist coactivation is another possible mechanism promoting ROM gains, through better adjusted force ratios. Also, some articles included in the meta-analysis assessed other outcomes in addition to ROM, and these indicated that ST programs may have additional advantages when compared to stretching, such as greater improvements in neck flexors endurance, ten repetition maximum Bench Press and Leg Press, and countermovement jump and 60-m sprint with hurdles which may favor the choice of ST over stretching interventions.

paragraphs.text_en: After protocol registration, we chose to improve upon the design, namely adding two dimensions (directness and imprecision) that would provide a complete GRADE assessment. Furthermore, subgroup analyses were not planned a priori. There is a risk of multiple subgroup analyses generating a false statistical difference, merely to the number of analyses conducted. However, all analyses showed an absence of significant differences and therefore provide a more complete understanding that the effects of ST or stretching on ROM are consistent across conditions. Looking backwards, perhaps removing the filters used in the initial searches could have provided a greater number of records. Notwithstanding, it would also likely provide a huge number of non-relevant records, including opinion papers and reviews. Moreover, consultation with four independent experts may hopefully have resolved this shortcoming.

segments.en: However, all analyses showed an absence of significant differences and therefore provide a more complete understanding that the effects of ST or stretching on ROM are consistent across conditions.

paragraphs.text_en: Due to the heterogeneity of populations analysed, sub-group analysis according to sex or age group were not possible, and so it would be important to explore if these features interact with the protocols in meaningful ways. Moreover, there was a predominance of studies with women, meaning more research with men is advised. There was also a predominance of assessments of hip joint ROM, followed by knee and shoulder, with the remaining joints receiving little to no attention. In addition, dose-response relationships could not be addressed, mainly due to poor reporting. However, the qualitative findings of all the studies were very homogeneous, with statistical significance tests failing to show differences between ST and stretching protocols.
